re_review_of: r0 (APPROVE with 3 minor gaps) after pessimistic r0 raised 4 CRITICALs
confirmed_criticals_resolved: CRITICAL-1 (coopmat shape metadata does not exist): RESOLVED and FEASIBLE. r1 plumbs the shape end-to-end in three steps that all build on already-existing code. (a) CoopMatKey gains k+result_type (mechanical struct extension; BTreeMap Ord determinism preserved by field-append). (b) CoopMatrixShape in coopmat.rs (line 219-226 today: {m,n,k,a_elem,b_elem,c_elem}) gains result_type+scope — additive only, no existing field removed. (c) KernelAnnotations gains coop_matrix: Option<CoopMatShape>; the existing cooperative_matrix: bool (hir.rs:101) is retained for back-compat — no existing code breaks. The lowering helper derive_coopmat_shape() extracts K=a.n(==b.m) from the M2.1-typechecked operand types, which already guarantee KDimMismatch is checked — no new validation needed. KernelMetadata gains #[serde(default)] coopmat field; CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION 1→2; load_kernel_metadata accepts {1,2} with v1 sidecars deserializing coopmat=None via serde(default). AT-1552 proves the runtime builds CoopMatRequiredShape from metadata (coopmat_required_shape_from_meta), nothing hardcoded — the HN-10/AT-1551 contradiction is resolved. The serde(default) approach is the standard Rust/serde pattern for additive schema evolution and is directly feasible with the existing serde+serde_json stack.

CRITICAL-2 (storageBuffer16BitAccess never enabled): RESOLVED and FEASIBLE. The required_device_features(binding_plan, uses_coopmat) pass correctly derives storage_16bit from binding_plan.buffers.any(needs_16bit_storage()) — not from coopmat-presence — so plain f16 SSBO kernels also get the feature. context.rs chains VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures{storageBuffer16BitAccess=VK_TRUE} when device-supported. The design calls out that this is the FIRST f16-SSBO dispatch ever and today context.rs enables only timelineSemaphore (confirmed: context.rs lines 192-210 show no 8/16-bit features). The fail-closed DeviceFeatureUnsupported skip prevents enable-and-hope. AT-1509 (pipeline-create-before-dispatch on NVIDIA) is the proof. Feasible against ash 0.38's VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures struct.

CRITICAL-3 (storageBuffer8BitAccess + shaderInt8 + shaderInt16 never enabled): RESOLVED and FEASIBLE via the same required_device_features pass. The binding-plan trigger (u8/i8 SSBO present → storage_8bit+shader_int8+shader_int16=true) is derivable from the existing BufferTy.elem field in ParamBindingPlan. context.rs chains VkPhysicalDevice8BitStorageFeatures + VkPhysicalDeviceShaderFloat16Int8Features + shaderInt16 (via base features or Vulkan11Features). AT-1522 (pipeline-create for q4km on NVIDIA) is the proof. The capability→feature table documents each row with the SPIR-V capability name, trigger, and Vulkan feature — this is exactly the auditing discipline the pessimist demanded.

CRITICAL-4 (no transpose-distinguishing fixture): RESOLVED and TECHNICALLY SOUND. The transpose_fixture_spec defines A[i][j]=f16(1.0+0.5i-0.25j) (row-gradient) and B[i][j]=f16(-0.5+0.5j+0.125i) (column-gradient). These are NOT symmetric (A[i][j]!=A[j][i]) and NOT equal to each other or each other's transpose. The worked-example analysis (AT-1512) asserts the four products A·B, Aᵀ·B, A·Bᵀ, B·A each differ by >10x the f16 tolerance. The magnitudes (|A|,|B|<=~8, K=16, |C|<=~few hundred) keep the inputs representable in f16 without large representation error while still producing asymmetric result surfaces. AT-1512 is a CPU-only guard (no GPU needed) that verifies the fixture is transpose-distinguishing before the dispatch test AT-1510 relies on it. This is structurally the correct approach — the fixture self-certifies its discriminating power.
confirmed_minor_gaps_closed: MINOR optimistic-1 (AT-1520 #[ignore]): CONFIRMED CLOSED. r1 revision_changelog entry explicitly states: 'AT-1520 (plain multi-row q4km matmul, no coopmat) is now a REGULAR GPU integration test (NOT #[ignore]); it runs on Lavapipe and NVIDIA under AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS=1.' AT-1520 acceptance test text confirms: 'NOT #[ignore] — runs as a normal GPU integration test' and 'cargo test -p axc-driver -- (AXC_ENABLE_GPU_TESTS=1; NOT --ignored)'. This directly closes the r0 concern that the 256x256 q4km matmul should run on Lavapipe CI without ignore gating.

MINOR optimistic-2 (pin q4km x/weight layout): CONFIRMED CLOSED. HN-11 gives a single definitive layout: q = n_rows consecutive weight-rows each n_blocks_per_row*144 bytes (Q4_K_M superblocks per M2.6); x = dense input matrix x[k*n_cols+col] column-of-output-major; y = row-major y[row*n_cols+col]. For the 256x256 fixture: n_rows=256, n_cols=256, n_blocks_per_row=1. CPU reference q4km_dequant_matmul_cpu matches this layout exactly. No fixture ambiguity remains.

MINOR optimistic-3 / pessimistic OQ-1 (subgroupSize==32 guard): CONFIRMED CLOSED. context.rs stores subgroup_size:u32 from VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Properties.subgroupSize; the matmul_tile dispatch path requires ctx.subgroup_size()==32 and returns DispatchError::CoopMatUnsupported with reason 'subgroup size N != 32 (matmul_tile is NVIDIA-32-lane-tuned)' for any wave64/SIMD16 device that might advertise the 16x16x16 shape. AT-1507 covers this. The debug interleaving guard (resident_bound: bool flag on KernelHandleInner, debug_assert only) is also specified per HN-8.
feasibility_checks: HIR CoopMatKey +2 fields: Pure struct extension. PartialOrd/Ord/Hash all derive — appending k:u32 and result_type:ScalarTy to the end of the struct preserves the existing field order in the derived Ord (field-declaration order in Rust). BTreeMap determinism is maintained. The codegen construction sites in body.rs/coopmat.rs are mechanical fill-from-already-known-local-variables. AT-1508 asserts SPIR-V word-count identity vs pre-M3.1 baseline — the key is internal dedup only, OpTypeCooperativeMatrixKHR operands are M/N/use/elem (unchanged). Feasible.

KernelMetadata schema 1→2 + serde(default): Standard serde pattern. Adding #[serde(default)] to a new Option<CoopMatShapeMeta> field means old JSON without the key deserializes to None — Rust serde documentation guarantees this. The load_kernel_metadata version check change (accept {1,2}) is a 2-line diff. The new CoopMatShapeMeta/CoopMatScalarMeta/CoopMatScopeMeta types are simple data structs with standard derives. KernelMetadata::with_coopmat(self, Option<CoopMatShapeMeta>) builder avoids churning every existing KernelMetadata::new() call site. Feasible with zero-risk backward compatibility.

required_device_features pass: Pure function over ParamBindingPlan (already available at all dispatch sites). The needs_16bit_storage() / needs_8bit_storage() helpers inspect BufferTy.elem (ScalarTy::F16 → 16-bit; ScalarTy::U8/I8 → 8-bit). The context.rs pNext chain assembly follows the existing vk12_features lifetime pattern (lines 192-210 show the pattern already established). Declaring all feature-struct locals at function scope solves the borrow-trap WARNING from the pessimist. ash 0.38 exposes VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures, VkPhysicalDevice8BitStorageFeatures, VkPhysicalDeviceShaderFloat16Int8Features — all present in ash since the Vulkan 1.1/1.2 structs landed (ash 0.37+). Feasible.

Preflight matcher (coopmat_shape_supported): Pure function over (CoopMatRequiredShape, CoopMatSupport). The matcher checks m/n/k + a/b/c/result component types + scope==Subgroup + saturatingAccumulation==false — all fields present in VkCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR. The two-call count idiom (count==0 → return empty, no second call) is the standard vkGet* pattern used throughout ash-based Vulkan code. Feasible.

GPU-resident benchmark (resident.rs): vkCmdWriteTimestamp + two-entry QueryPool(TIMESTAMP) is the canonical Vulkan timing pattern, available since Vulkan 1.0 (spec §18.5). The N-loop single-allocation CB+fence+query-pool reuse pattern is straightforward — one vk::CommandPool allocation outside the loop, reset+rerecord or pre-record once per the N calls. masked_timestamp_delta(begin,end,valid_bits) = ((begin & mask) as u64).wrapping_sub((end & mask) as u64) ... actually end.wrapping_sub(begin) after masking both — a 3-line function tested by AT-1535. Query pool lifetime in ResidentBuffers::drop is explicit in the spec. Feasible.

Lever A re-land (binding_is_readback): A 3-line predicate. Applied uniformly in all four readback loops per HN-9. The four-loop uniformity requirement was the exact M3.0 r2 lesson; the design explicitly references it. Feasible.

Transpose-distinguishing fixture: f16 arithmetic on values in [-1,8] range is representable in f16 (half-precision covers ±65504 with ~3 significant decimal digits). Row/column gradient matrices with different slopes produce asymmetric dot-product surfaces. The 10x tolerance margin check in AT-1512 is a CPU-only assertion that takes microseconds. Feasible.

No new codegen emission: The spec states SPIR-V capabilities are ALL already emitted by M2.1/M2.6 (confirmed in coopmat.rs and emit.rs per the pessimist's code-reading). M3.1 is exclusively runtime + metadata + kernels. spirv-val (AT-1511/AT-1560) continues to validate the MODULE; the new AT-1509/AT-1522 pipeline-create tests validate the RUNTIME FEATURE WIRING. Scope is clean and correct.

scope_preservation_check.public_api_preserved: All existing public API and bench IDs confirmed preserved. VulkanContextOptions gains force_no_coopmat: Option<bool> (Default=None — backward-compatible with struct-update syntax). KernelMetadata gains coopmat via with_coopmat builder — existing ::new() callers unchanged. DispatchError gains 2 new variants (count 28→30); at_801 keeps its name with bumped count — same precedent as prior milestone bumps.
scope_preservation_check.bench_ids_preserved: dispatch_resident_matmul_tile and matmul_tflops_4096 are NEW bench IDs. No existing bench IDs renamed or removed.
scope_preservation_check.scope_honesty: Staged q4km-coopmat split retained. shared[T,N] deferred to M3.2. cuBLAS comparison labeled 'estimate (external cuBLAS baseline)', only effective TFLOPS asserted (AT-1532). NVIDIA runner mandatory gate stated explicitly in acceptance_gate. All consistent with r0 scope decisions.
scope_preservation_check.no_regression_surface: CoopMatKey struct extension is internal cache-key only; emitted SPIR-V word-count identical (AT-1508). KernelMetadata schema v1 sidecars continue to deserialize. Lever A re-land has AT-1541 regression guard (existing q4km/saxpy tests). All existing module-level tests unaffected.

additional_observations: The capability→feature table (capability_to_feature_table) is exactly the right artifact — it maps each emitted SPIR-V capability to its Vulkan device feature in a machine-readable form with both trigger conditions and runtime actions documented. This resolves the pessimist's 'implicit feature acquisition' principle violation and the optimistic reviewer's validation request. Reference: matches the methodology in Khronos VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec Table 1 (per-feature mapping). External ref: https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix.html

The shaderFloat16 row in the capability→feature table correctly notes it is NOT required by M3.1 kernels: matmul_tile uses f16 inside coopmat ops (covered by cooperativeMatrix feature), and q4km converts f16→f32 immediately via OpFConvert (no scalar f16 ALU). This is a subtle correctness distinction that the spec gets right. Reference: Vulkan spec §53.1 VkPhysicalDeviceShaderFloat16Int8Features — shaderFloat16 governs scalar f16 arithmetic, not storage or coopmat accumulation.

The warning about pNext chain lifetime (all feature-struct locals at function scope) is explicitly resolved in vulkan_features_extensions.feature_chain_assembly: 'All feature-struct locals are declared at function scope (NOT inside the timeline+1.2 if-branch)'. This is the correct fix for the borrow-lifetime trap the pessimist identified. The current context.rs (lines 192-210) shows vk12_features is already at function scope — the extension to additional feature structs follows the same pattern.

AT-1501 coverage of count==0 two-call guard is explicitly noted: 'AT-1501 extended to cover ext-present-but-count==0'. The two-call idiom guard (don't call the second properties function if count==0) is correct per the Vulkan vkGet* idiom spec §4.1.1.

AT-1561 extended to cover result_type and saturatingAccumulation near-miss rejection per the pessimist WARNING. Combined with the result_type field now on CoopMatKey and CoopMatRequiredShape (sourced from metadata.coopmat.result_type), the near-miss rejection is now architecturally grounded, not just a test-side check.
strengths: Complete HIR→metadata→runtime shape plumbing resolves the CRITICAL-1 self-contradiction (HN-10 'not a literal' vs missing metadata). The chosen approach (derive shape from typechecked operand types in lower.rs) reuses existing type-safety guarantees — no new validation surface to get wrong.

The required_device_features() pass as a pure function of (binding_plan, uses_coopmat) is the correct abstraction: it is testable without a GPU (AT-1504), it is deterministic, and it separates capability derivation from the Vulkan chain-assembly complexity in context.rs. This matches the 'annotations are first-class data' AXIOM-Compute thesis — the binding plan IS the capability declaration.

Fail-closed discipline throughout: DeviceFeatureUnsupported for missing storage/int features, CoopMatUnsupported for shape/scope/subgroup mismatch, both typed DispatchError variants. No enable-and-hope path exists in the spec.

The mandatory NVIDIA runner gate in acceptance_gate ('AT-1510 skipping on EVERY available device is a milestone FAIL, not a pass') directly addresses anti-pattern #9 (no mocking GPU execution in tests). force_no_coopmat (AT-1506) exercises the skip path on NVIDIA without substituting for the dispatch proof.

Metadata schema back-compat is zero-risk: serde(default) on an Option field is the canonical Rust approach, used widely in the ecosystem (e.g., serde_json docs §Default). AT-1553 covers both directions. Existing M0..M2.6 test corpus sidecars (schema_version=1) will continue to work.
concerns: Informational only (not a blocking concern): The spec defers the query for VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Properties.subgroupSize to context init, but does not specify whether it uses VkPhysicalDeviceSubgroupProperties (Vulkan 1.1 core via vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2) or VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Properties (Vulkan 1.2+ inlined struct). Either is correct (they report the same value), but the Coder should note that on Vulkan 1.1 devices the inlined Vulkan11Properties struct is not available — use the standalone SubgroupProperties. Not a blocker; documented in HN-4 (subgroup_size: u32 from VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Properties OR VkPhysicalDeviceSubgroupProperties).

Informational only: The spec does not explicitly say whether coopmat_required_shape_from_meta (converting CoopMatShapeMeta → CoopMatRequiredShape) is tested independently. AT-1552 covers the end-to-end path (compile → metadata → runtime reads shape), which is sufficient. A narrow unit test of the conversion function itself (CoopMatScalarMeta::F16 → CoopMatComponentType::Float16) would be belt-and-suspenders but is not required for approval.
validation_against_existing: coopmat.rs (lines 206-211 confirmed): CoopMatKey today is {elem, m, n, use_} — NO k, NO result_type. r1 adds both. The BTreeMap usage in codegen body.rs/coopmat.rs is confirmed — the struct-append Ord rule (Rust derives Ord by field declaration order) means the new fields sort after existing fields, preserving relative ordering of existing keys. No cache invalidation needed.

metadata.rs (lines 35, 45-68 confirmed): CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION=1, KernelMetadata has 6 fields, no coopmat. r1 adds field 7 (coopmat: Option<CoopMatShapeMeta>) with serde(default). Serde guarantees this is backward-compatible: https://serde.rs/attr-default.html. at_503 will be updated to assert schema_version==2.

context.rs (lines 87-118, 192-210 confirmed): VulkanContextOptions has 5 fields (all Option); force_no_coopmat is the 6th, Default=None, backward-compatible. VulkanContext body shows no coopmat-related fields today — r1 adds coopmat_support, enabled_features, timestamp_period, compute_timestamp_valid_bits, subgroup_size.

SPV_KHR_cooperative_matrix spec §3 confirms: VkCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR includes MSize, NSize, KSize, AType, BType, CType, ResultType, scope, saturatingAccumulation — all fields the r1 matcher checks. https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VkCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR.html

Khronos Vulkan-Samples cooperative_matrix sample (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/tree/main/samples/extensions/cooperative_matrix) enables: VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix extension + VkPhysicalDeviceCooperativeMatrixFeaturesKHR.cooperativeMatrix + VkPhysicalDeviceVulkanMemoryModelFeatures.vulkanMemoryModel + VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures.storageBuffer16BitAccess for f16 SSBOs — exactly the feature set r1 specifies for CRITICAL-1/-2.

VK_KHR_16bit_storage spec: 'storageBuffer16BitAccess: Specifies whether objects in the StorageBuffer, ShaderRecordBufferKHR, or PhysicalStorageBuffer storage class with the Block decoration can have 16-bit integer and 16-bit floating-point members.' This is precisely the feature needed for f16 SSBO bindings. https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures.html

VK_KHR_8bit_storage spec: 'storageBuffer8BitAccess: Specifies whether objects in the StorageBuffer...storage class...can have 8-bit integer members.' Required for u8 SSBO (q4km path). https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-extensions/man/html/VkPhysicalDevice8BitStorageFeatures.html
external_references: Vulkan spec §18.5 Timestamp Queries (vkCmdWriteTimestamp + timestampPeriod + valid_bits): https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/1.3-khr-extensions/html/vkspec.html#queries-timestamps
serde #[serde(default)] for additive schema evolution: https://serde.rs/attr-default.html
test_suggestions: No mandatory additions. The AT-1509 (pipeline-create-before-dispatch) suggestion from r0 has been incorporated as a mandatory AT. The AT-1512 (transpose-fixture self-certification) suggestion from the pessimist has been incorporated. AT-1535 (timestamp boundary) is now present. AT-1553 (metadata v1/v2 back-compat) is new and correct.

Optional belt-and-suspenders: a narrow unit test of CoopMatScalarMeta → CoopMatComponentType conversion in coopmat_required_shape_from_meta would ensure no enum-variant mismatch between the HIR and runtime type systems. AT-1552 covers the end-to-end path, so this is not required.

Optional: AT-1507 covers the subgroupSize guard via the pure predicate; a runner-level assertion that NVIDIA (subgroup_size=32) does NOT skip for this reason would close the loop completely. This is noted in the AT-1507 description ('plus a runner assertion that NVIDIA (size 32) does NOT skip for this reason') — confirm the Coder includes it.
summary: All four CRITICALs from the pessimistic r0 review are resolved in r1 with feasible, well-specified solutions: CRITICAL-1 (coopmat shape metadata) is plumbed HIR→codegen→metadata→runtime end-to-end using serde(default) and existing typecheck guarantees; CRITICAL-2/-3 (16/8-bit storage and Int8/Int16 features) are addressed by the required_device_features() binding-plan-driven pass with fail-closed DeviceFeatureUnsupported skip; CRITICAL-4 (transpose fixture) is addressed by a mathematically sound non-symmetric 16x16 fixture with AT-1512 self-certification. All three r0 minor gaps are also closed: AT-1520 is non-#[ignore], q4km layout is pinned in HN-11, and the debug interleaving guard (resident_bound flag) is specified. Scope, honesty, public API, and bench IDs are preserved. The NVIDIA runner mandatory gate is now explicit in acceptance_gate. No feasibility regressions introduced.
